scan_metadata.paper: Bayer et al. (2023), Nature Communications 14(1), 7902, doi:10.1038/s41467-023-43696-z
scan_metadata.explanation: Of the requested scope, only the three example_datasets/ worked examples (decryptM_Dasatinib, kinobeads_Dasatinib, viability_CTRP_40) supply a real, complete, traceable (input + toml + reference output) Mode-1 CLI execution, and together they back a single exposed tool, run_dose_response_pipeline, owned by the cli_wrapper module. example_toml_files/ and example_api_usage/ matched the requested filter but yielded no additional tool (see tutorial-scanner.json's tool_review for the full reasoning: reference-only TOML templates with no companion input data, and notebooks that use the Python library API rather than the CLI).

suggested_tools.description: Runs the CurveCurator dose-response pipeline end-to-end on one parameters.toml: fits a 4-parameter logistic model per curve, applies SAM-style significance/relevance thresholding, optionally estimates FDR via target-decoy simulation (--fdr) and/or runs MAD-based noisy-channel detection (--mad), and renders the interactive bokeh dashboard.
suggested_tools.primary_input: Path to a completed parameters.toml file (its own [Paths].input_file, relative to the toml's directory, names the raw MaxQuant/DIA-NN/PD/MSFragger search-engine output or plain viability .tsv); optional estimate_fdr and run_mad booleans.
suggested_tools.outputs: curves.txt (per-curve pEC50, Curve Slope/Front/Back, Curve Fold Change, Curve F_Value, Curve P_Value, Curve Relevance Score, Curve Regulation, etc.), dashboard.html, curveCurator.log, and when requested decoys_file+fdr_file (--fdr) or mad_file (--mad), at the paths the toml declares.

suggested_tools.description: Same tool as above, validated on a second, independent input/measurement type (MaxQuant proteinGroups.txt, LFQ protein-level) to confirm the pipeline generalizes across the documented search-engine input formats.
suggested_tools.primary_input: Path to parameters.toml whose [Paths].input_file points to proteinGroups.txt; optional estimate_fdr and run_mad booleans.
suggested_tools.outputs: curves.txt, dashboard.html, curveCurator.log (and decoys_file/fdr_file or mad_file if requested).

suggested_tools.description: Same tool as above, validated on the non-proteomics viability data path (measurement_type/data_type/search_engine='OTHER') with control_fold_change and interpolation enabled; confirms the wrapper must honor whatever curves_file/dashboard output paths the toml declares (this example uses a '_40.0' suffix) rather than assuming fixed output filenames.
suggested_tools.primary_input: Path to parameters_40.0.toml whose [Paths].input_file points to dose_responses_40.0.tsv; optional estimate_fdr and run_mad booleans.
suggested_tools.outputs: curves_40.0.txt, dashboard_40.0.html, curveCurator.log (and decoys_file/fdr_file or mad_file if requested).
